title: Customer Experience Quarterly Review — Deck Kit & Renewal Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This single-file kit is a lightweight, modular set of slide templates, speaker notes, and a renewal-tracker scaffold for Customer Success managers running quarterly business reviews (QBRs) for both Standard and Enterprise accounts. The goal is to make each meeting concise, action-oriented, and tailored to the customer’s deployment type (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

How to use this kit:
- Choose the variant (Standard vs Enterprise) that matches the customer tier.
- Pull metrics from the Dashboard (tokens, latency, error rate, spends by route/model).
- Populate the renewal tracker during the meeting; capture commitments and next steps.
- Use the playbook checklist to escalate at-risk accounts and to prepare enablement tasks post QBR.

Quick note on data pulls (prep):
- Metrics to fetch before the meeting: monthly token usage (by model), average and p95 request latency, model version distribution, errors by route, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, autoscale events, recent rollouts (timestamps).
- Where: Redwood Console -> Customer -> Usage -> Export CSV. Also grab the last 3 eval run results (quality regressions).

STANDARD VARIANT (30–40 minute customer-facing deck)
Slide 1 — Title / Meeting Objectives
- Title: Quarterly Review • [Customer Name] • [Quarter Year]
- Objectives (bullets): Align on success metrics, review consumption & value, identify risk/opportunity, agree on top 3 priorities to next quarter.
Speaker note: Set expectations: 30–40 mins + 10 mins for next steps. Confirm if additional stakeholders need deeper dive.

Slide 2 — Executive Snapshot (1-slide summary)
- 3 headline bullets: Health (green/amber/red), ARR motion impact, renewal status (on-track / at-risk).
Speaker note: Keep it high level. Use this for execs who will leave early.

Slide 3 — Usage & Value Summary
- Graphs: tokens/month (3-month), top 3 routes by spend, top models used.
- Quick interpretation: Where value is coming from (search, chat, embeddings).

Slide 4 — Performance & Reliability
- Metrics: avg latency, p95, errors, cache hit rate.
- Notable incidents in quarter with impact and mitigation.

Slide 5 — Cost Efficiency & Optimization Opportunities
- Current cost per 1k tokens, suggestions (batching, prefix cache, lower-cost model variant, quantization).
- Estimated cost savings if applied (conservative / aggressive).

Slide 6 — Product/Feature Adoption
- Adoption of features: streaming, function-calls, embeddings.
- Roadmap items relevant to their use (e.g., dedicated autoscaling policy changes).

Slide 7 — Risks & Mitigations
- Bulleted risks (latency spikes, model regressions, quota constraints) + owner + timeline.

Slide 8 — Top 3 Priorities (for next quarter)
- Explicit owner, success metric, due date.

Slide 9 — Renewal & Commercial Signals
- Contract end date, usage trend vs committed, forecasted overage, negotiation windows.

Slide 10 — Action Summary & Next Steps
- 3–5 concrete actions, who owns them, by when. Close with ask: decision point for renewal.

ENTERPRISE VARIANT (45–60 minute, deeper technical + exec split)
Slide 1 — Executive Overview (single slide for execs)
- Value delivered in $ or efficiency metrics, strategic alignment, renewal outlook.

Slide 2 — Compliance & Security Posture
- Deployment type (VPC, on-prem), KMS/HSM integration status, recent audits, open security items.
Speaker note: Enterprise customers expect this early in the deck.

Slide 3 — Architecture & Traffic Patterns
- Diagram: edge -> routing policy -> model pool (hosted/dedicated) -> cache.
- Notes on fallback policies and cross-region DR.

Slide 4 — SLOs, Observability & Incident Review
- SLO attainment (monthly), tracing highlights, top 3 incidents root cause + RCA links.

Slide 5 — Cost Engineering & Unit Economics
- Per-feature token costs, per-endpoint latency SLOs, suggestions: dedicated/reserved vs burst.

Slide 6 — Model Quality & Governance
- Eval results, regression alerts, canary rollout outcomes, model pinning recommendations.

Slide 7 — Custom Integrations & Roadmap Alignment
- Any customizations, upcoming infra changes that could impact them (e.g., new allocator / compilation kernels).

Slide 8 — Renewal Strategy (commercial options)
- Options table: renew as-is, upsell to reserved capacity, move to private deployment, pre-pay discounts.

Slide 9 — Risk & Strategic Playbook
- Risk scorecard, mitigation plan, legal/compliance dependencies, exec sponsors.

Slide 10 — Commitments & Governance Cadence
- Quarterly steering committee schedule, SLAs, escalation path.

Supplemental slides (both variants, add as appendix)
- Detailed usage by route (CSV), raw incident timeline, evaluation result links, technical runbook excerpts.

RENEWAL TRACKER (copy into a sheet during the meeting)
- Suggested columns (CSV header line):
  customer, contract_id, renewal_date, mrr_current, committed_tokens, last_3mo_avg_tokens, forecasted_tokens_12mo, renewal_status, commercial_option, owner, next_step, next_step_due, risk_score, notes

Example CSV line:
  "Acme Corp","CNT-2022-11","2026-06-30","$12,500","1,000,000","1,200,000","14,400,000","at-risk","reserved-upsell","A.Chen","2026-03-10","7","Customer running higher throughput; needs cost model"

RISK SCORING RUBRIC (use 0-10, 10 highest risk)
- 0-3: Healthy — usage >= commit, no incidents, engaged weekly.
- 4-6: Watch — usage variance, 1 minor incident, delayed enablement tasks.
- 7-10: At-risk — sustained drop vs commit, major incident, executive churn or procurement delays.
- Risk contributors (additive): usage gap (>20% below commit add 3), active incident within 30 days add 2, security/compliance open item add 3, billing dispute add 2.

QBR PLAYBOOK: PRE, DURING, POST
Pre-meeting (72–48 hours)
- Data: export usage, incidents, last evals, recent PRs; ask customer for any internal attendee list and priorities.
- Internal: sync with Solutions/SE if custom infra touched in quarter.
- Prepare 1-pager exec snapshot + printed renewal tracker.
During meeting
- Start with exec snapshot (2–3 mins).
- Run through usage & value (8–10 mins standard, 15–20 enterprise).
- Surface 3 priorities and confirm owners. Fill renewal tracker live.
Post-meeting (24–72 hours)
- Send meeting notes + action items and calendar invites for any follow-ups.
- Update renewal tracker in shared sheet and tag AE/AM and Solutions.
- If risk_score >= 7, open an "at-risk" Slack channel and schedule weekly check-ins.

ESCALATION MATRIX (quick)
- CSM -> AM -> Solutions Team -> Escalation Lead (CS Director) -> Legal/Finance.
- Trigger conditions: risk_score >= 7, P1 incident unresolved > 48 hours, security gap flagged by audit.

SAMPLE EMAIL TEMPLATES
1) Meeting invite (short)
Subject: QBR — [Customer] — [Quarter], proposed agenda
Body: Hi [Name], would love to run a 40-min quarterly review to share usage, performance, and key opportunities. Proposed agenda attached. Please confirm attendees.

2) Post-meeting summary (action-focused)
Subject: QBR follow-up & next steps — [Customer] 
Body: Thanks for your time. Summary attached. Key actions: (1) [action] owner [x] due [dd], (2) [action] owner [y] due [dd]. Renewal status: [on-track/at-risk].

TEMPLATES & ASSETS (where to grab)
- Slide master: /shared-drives/customer-success/slides/qbr-slide-master.pptx (link to internal slide repo).
- Data export guide: Redwood Console -> Usage -> Export (link internal doc).
- Risk playbook and at-risk Slack template: /shared-drives/customer-success/playbooks/at-risk-playbook.md

Notes on tailoring for Redwood product signals (use these callouts in slides)
- Show dedicated vs hosted cost differential if they are nearing commit for Dedicated.
- If private deployment: highlight compliance milestones and HSM/KMS status.
- Point out any recent Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization) and estimated savings.
- Call out model pinning and canary rollout results if a regression was detected.

Final checklist before sharing deck
- [ ] Refresh metrics (within 48 hours).
- [ ] Confirm attendee list & exec asks.
- [ ] Attach linked artifacts: incident RCAs, eval runs, contract summary.
- [ ] Save a copy of the populated renewal tracker in the account folder.

Appendix: short glossary for execs
- Token: unit of billing.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity for consistent throughput.
- Private: customer-hosted or VPC deployment with customer-managed networking.
- Eval: automatic or manual quality check for model output.

End of kit.

Document history:
- 2025-11-18: first draft by A. Chen.
- 2026-01-11: added enterprise compliance slide and sample CSV.
- 2026-02-28: refined risk rubric and playbook steps (L. Rodriguez).
